'''U. K. Anandavardhanan''' (born 25 May 1976) is an Indian mathematician specialising in  [[automorphic form]]s and [[representation theory]]. He was awarded the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology]], the highest science award in India, for the year 2020 in mathematical science category.<ref>{{cite web |title=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize (SSB) for Science and Technology 2020 List of recipients |url=https://ssbprize.gov.in/WriteReadData/LatestUpdates/202009260117197601874ShantiSwarupBhatnagarPrize2020Website.pdf |website=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology |publisher=[[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research|CSIR]] Human Resource Development Group, New Delhi |access-date=28 September 2020}}</ref> He is affiliated to [[Indian Institute of Technology, Bombay]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Two IIT-Bombay profs, BARC researcher bag India’s coveted science award |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/two-iit-bombay-profs-barc-researcher-bag-indias-coveted-science-award/articleshow/78357996.cms |access-date=3 October 2020 |agency=The Times of India |date=28 September 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Anonna Dutt |title=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize 2020: 12 researchers receive India’s highest science award |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/science/shanti-swarup-bhatnagar-prize-2020-12-researchers-receive-india-s-highest-science-award/story-mpguVPsNq7U60SY8fnXo4K.html |access-date=3 October 2020 |agency=Hindusthan times |date=26 September 2020}}</ref>

After completing undergraduate studies in [[University of Calicut]], Anandavardhanan joined [[University of Hyderabad]] for further studies. He secured M Sc in mathematics from there in 1998 and Ph D in 2003. He was with Tata Institute of Fundamental Research during February 2003 - July 2005 and spent the spring of 2004 in University of Iowa. He has been a faculty member of Indian Institute of Technology Bombay since July 2005.
